# Visual Studio Code Interface Description

## System and Window Information

- **Operating System**: Linux (based on desktop environment and application icons)
- **Application**: Visual Studio Code
- **Window Title**: Settings - Visual Studio Code
- **Date and Time**: Oct 23 00:38
- **Window Controls**: Minimize, Maximize, Close buttons in top-right corner
- **Application Icon**: VS Code logo in top-left corner
- **Activities Menu**: Visible in top-left corner
- **System Tray**: Visible in top-right corner with volume and power icons

## Top Menu Bar

- **Menu Items**: File, Edit, Selection, View, Go, Run, Terminal, Help
- **Active Tab**: Settings (highlighted with a blue underline)
- **Tab Close Button**: "X" next to Settings tab

## Left Sidebar (Activity Bar)

- **Icons (Top to Bottom)**:
  - **File Explorer Icon**: Currently active (highlighted)
  - **Search Icon**
  - **Source Control Icon**
  - **Debug Icon**
  - **Extensions Icon**
  - **Git Icon**
  - **Terminal Icon**
  - **Settings Icon** (with notification badge "1")
  - **Outline Icon**
  - **Timeline Icon**
  - **Grid Icon** (Application launcher)
  - **User Icon**
  - **Gear Icon** (Settings)

## Explorer Panel

- **Status**: "NO FOLDER OPENED"
- **Message**: "You have not yet opened a folder."
- **Action Buttons**:
  - **Open Folder**: Blue button
  - **Clone Repository**: Blue button
- **Additional Information**:
  - "Opening a folder will close all currently open editors. To keep them open, add a folder instead."
  - "You can clone a repository locally."
  - "To learn more about how to use Git and source control in VS Code read our docs."

## Main Content Area

### Settings Tab

- **Active Section**: "User" (highlighted)
- **Settings Categories**:
  - Workbench (1)
  - Window (1)
  - Features (1)
  - Extensions (1)
  - Security (4)
  - Workspace (4)
- **Search Bar**: "workspace trust ena" (partial text)
- **Search Results**: "7 Settings Found" with filter icon
- **Action Button**: "Backup and Sync Settings" (blue button)

### Settings Details

#### Security > Workspace > Trust: Enabled

- **Description**: "Controls whether or not Workspace Trust is enabled within VS Code."
- **Checkbox**: Checked (enabled)
- **Note**: "(Applies to all profiles)"

#### Workbench > Trusted Domains: Prompt In Trusted Workspace

- **Description**: "When enabled, trusted domain prompts will appear when opening links in trusted workspaces."
- **Checkbox**: Unchecked (disabled)
- **Note**: "(Applies to all profiles)"

#### Extensions: Support Untrusted Workspaces

- **Description**: "Override the untrusted workspace support of an extension. Extensions using true will always be enabled. Extensions using limited will always be enabled, and the extension will hide functionality that requires trust. Extensions using false will only be enabled only when the workspace is trusted."
- **Action Link**: "Edit in settings.json"

#### Window: Title

- **Description**: "Controls the window title based on the current context such as the opened workspace or active editor. Variables are substituted based on the context:"
- **Variables List**:
  - `${activeEditorShort}`: the file name (e.g. myFile.txt)
  - `${activeEditorMedium}`: the path of the file relative to the workspace folder (e.g. myFolder/myFileFolder/myFile.txt)
  - `${activeEditorLong}`: the full path of the file (e.g. /Users/Development/myFolder/myFileFolder/myFile.txt)
  - `${activeFolderShort}`: the name of the folder the file is contained in (e.g. myFileFolder)
  - `${activeFolderMedium}`: the path of the folder the file is contained in, relative to the workspace folder (e.g. myFolder/myFileFolder)
  - `${activeFolderLong}`: the full path of the folder the file is contained in (e.g. /Users/Development/myFolder/myFileFolder)
  - `${folderName}`: name of the workspace folder the file is contained in (e.g. myFolder)
  - `${folderPath}`: file path of the workspace folder the file is contained in (e.g. /Users/Development/myFolder)
  - `${rootName}`: name of the workspace with optional remote name and workspace indicator if applicable (e.g. myFolder, myRemoteFolder [SSH] or myWorkspace (Workspace))
  - `${rootNameShort}`: shortened name of the workspace without suffixes (e.g. myFolder, myRemoteFolder
